references.text: The people repeat the same prayer to Moses at Horeb, asking him to be an intermediary between them and God because they fear dying if they hear God's voice directly.
Moses reminds the people that they asked not to hear God's voice directly at Horeb because they feared death.
Describes the people's fear when God revealed Himself on Mount Sinai with thunder, lightning, and a loud trumpet sound.
The preceding verse describing the people's reaction to God's presence—they trembled and kept their distance.
The Letter to the Hebrews refers to this event and describes how the Israelites could not endure God's presence and asked that no more words be spoken to them.
Paul mentions that the law was given through an intermediary (Moses), pointing back to the people's wish for Moses to speak to them instead of God.
Moses confirms his role as mediator between the Lord and the people because they were afraid of the fire and did not go up the mountain.
Theological contrast between the people's fear of God's face and Moses' demand that this very face must be with them.
A parallel highlighting the people's ambivalent attitude toward God's direct speech: first fearing it (Ex 20), later resenting Moses' role in it (Num 12).
Direct contextual link: God's warning (19:21) about the people's fear and death (20:19) are two sides of the same event.
Theological contrast between the people's rejection of truth (Isaiah) and their fear of meeting God directly (Exodus).
A deep theological parallel concerning humanity's fear and desire to avoid God's direct presence and demands.
